read_ranges.scope: entire text: definitions, all main results and proofs, compressed sensing/empirical process/chaos applications, appendix lemmas and references

topic_relevance.K03: direct: Theorem 3.5 proves mixed subgaussian-subexponential tail chaining with separate gamma_2/gamma_1 complexity and separate square-root/linear deviation scales; Sections 5–6 give empirical-process and chaos applications.
topic_relevance.H05: adjacent: uses Bernstein/Hanson–Wright single-increment tail inputs inside the chaining proof; it does not replace the need to prove those increment bounds for a target process.
topic_relevance.K05: adjacent: cites Talagrand generic chaining and majorizing measures, but the target result is a mixed-tail chaining inequality, not a standalone convex-concentration theorem.

definitions.name: psi_alpha increment process
definitions.statement: For a semi-metric d, P(||X_t-X_s|| >= u d(t,s)) <= 2 exp(-u^alpha), u>=0; gamma_alpha(T,d) is the infimum of the supremum chaining sum over admissible sequences with |T_0|=1 and |T_n|<=2^(2^n).

definitions.name: mixed tail
definitions.statement: For two semi-metrics d_1,d_2, P(||X_t-X_s|| >= sqrt(u)d_2(t,s)+u d_1(t,s)) <= 2 exp(-u), for all s,t and u>=0.

definitions.name: truncated gamma functional and base-point term
definitions.statement: gamma_{alpha,p} truncates the admissible chaining sum below l=floor(log_2 p); the Lp theorem also retains 2 sup_t (E||X_t-X_t0||^p)^(1/p).

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 3.5 (mixed-tail chaining)
assumptions: T is finite in the proof; the paper states the extension to infinite T using lattice suprema over finite subsets.
For every s,t in T, the mixed-tail increment condition (12) holds for semi-metrics d_1,d_2.
1<=p<infinity for the moment bound; u>=1 for the tail bound.
theorem_cards.statement: There are universal constants C,c>0 such that (E sup_t ||X_t-X_t0||^p)^(1/p) <= C(gamma_2(T,d_2)+gamma_1(T,d_1))+2 sup_t(E||X_t-X_t0||^p)^(1/p). Consequently, P{sup_t ||X_t-X_t0|| >= C(gamma_2+gamma_1)+c(sqrt(u) Delta_{d_2}(T)+u Delta_{d_1}(T))} <= exp(-u).
proof_steps: Choose admissible partitions B,C near-optimal for gamma'_2(T,d_2) and gamma'_1(T,d_1); intersect level-shifted partitions to obtain one admissible chain, then choose representatives pi_n(t).

Split X_t-X_t0 into the base approximation X_{pi_l(t)}-X_t0 and the telescoping increments over n>l, with l=floor(log_2 p). The base term is bounded using the finite cardinality of the l-th net and its Lp norm.

Apply the mixed-tail assumption to each pair (pi_n(t),pi_{n-1}(t)); count at most 2^(2^(n+1)) pairs and union-bound across levels, obtaining a good event with complement at most c exp(-p u/4) for u>=2.

On the good event, sum the two increment contributions separately: sqrt(u) times the d_2 chaining sum and u times the d_1 chaining sum. Compare gamma-prime and gamma functionals to obtain the moment bound.
Use the pointwise mixed-tail moment estimate for the base increments, then the paper's moment-to-tail lemma to derive the stated diameter terms and probability exp(-u).
gaps: The proof does not optimize numerical constants; the paper explicitly notes losses in the moment/tail conversion.

For uncountable T, measurability is not automatic; the stated interpretation is a lattice supremum, and a target application must establish separability/measurability if it needs an ordinary sample supremum.
No independence of increments is required, but every pairwise mixed-tail increment bound must still be established for the target process.

theorem_cards.label: Corollary 5.2 (unbounded empirical processes)
assumptions: For each i, X_{t i} are measurable subexponential variables on independent probability spaces; across i the summands are independent.
Uniform Bernstein moment condition: m^(-1) sum_i E|X_{t i}-E X_{t i}|^q <= (q!/2) sigma^2 K^(q-2) for every t and integer q>=2.
The metrics are d_1(s,t)=max_i ||X_{t i}-X_{s i}||_{psi_1} and d_2(s,t)=(m^(-1)sum_i ||X_{t i}-X_{s i}||_{psi_1}^2)^(1/2).
theorem_cards.statement: For E_t=m^(-1)sum_i(X_{t i}-E X_{t i}), the theorem gives an Lp bound with chaining terms m^(-1/2)gamma_2(T,d_2)+m^(-1)gamma_1(T,d_1), plus sigma sqrt(p/m)+pK/m; the tail form has sqrt(u) sigma/sqrt(m)+uK/m and probability at most exp(-u), up to absolute constants.
proof_steps: Apply Bernstein's inequality to each centered increment E_t-E_s, obtaining the mixed-tail condition with the displayed d_1,d_2 scales.
Substitute those scaled metrics into Theorem 3.5 and simplify gamma functionals by homogeneity.
Retain the uniform Bernstein parameters sigma,K; they control the single-index/base-point terms as well as deviations.
gaps: The independence assumption is across the summands i; the result does not automatically extend to dependent observations without another Bernstein-type increment theorem.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 5.5 (supremum of averages of squares)
assumptions: For each i, X_{t i} are subgaussian and independent across i; T is finite for the chaining proof.
Averages A_t=m^(-1)sum_i(X_{t i}^2-E X_{t i}^2) obey the uniform Bernstein moment condition (28) with parameters sigma,K.
The chaining metric is d_{psi_2}(s,t)=max_i ||X_{s i}-X_{t i}||_{psi_2}; the radius Delta-bar_{psi_2}=sup_{t,i}||X_{t i}||_{psi_2} is finite.
theorem_cards.statement: For 1<=p<infinity, the Lp norm of sup_t |A_t| is bounded, up to absolute constants, by m^(-1)gamma_{2,p}^2(T,d_{psi_2}) + (Delta-bar_{psi_2}/sqrt(m))gamma_{2,p}(T,d_{psi_2}) + sigma sqrt(p/m)+pK/m. The corresponding tail bound replaces p by u in the last two scales and uses full gamma_2, with probability <= exp(-u).
proof_steps: Split the chaining levels into subgaussian levels and subexponential levels at 2^(n/2) approximately sqrt(m); establish increment bounds for A_t in the first range and for the empirical L2 distance in the second.
On a union-bound good event, telescope A_t along an optimal gamma_{2,p} net; use Cauchy-Schwarz to control differences of squares by empirical L2 increments times square-root process size.
Solve the resulting quadratic inequality in (sup_t |A_t|)^(1/2), then convert the increment tail estimate to an Lp bound.
Control the coarse net with the uniform Bernstein condition (28), completing the Lp estimate; the appendix moment-tail lemma yields the deviation form.
gaps: The subgaussianity of X_{t i} alone is not the whole hypothesis: the centered squares also need the uniform Bernstein moment condition (28), which the paper notes can be taken from uniform psi_2 bounds with explicit sigma,K choices.

theorem_cards.label: Theorem 6.5 (second-order chaos application)
assumptions: Xi are independent, mean-zero real variables with finite psi_2 norms; A is a set of m-by-n matrices.
The proof uses Hanson-Wright tails, decoupling, symmetrization and the matrix metric d_infinity(A,B)=||A-B||_{S_infinity}.
The theorem is stated for 1<=p<infinity; the tail consequence for u>=1.
theorem_cards.statement: The supremum of centered squared norms ||A xi||_2^2-E||A xi||_2^2 has an Lp bound controlled by gamma_{2,p}^2(A,d_infinity)+Delta-bar_2(A)gamma_{2,p}(A,d_infinity)+sqrt(p)Delta-bar_4^2(A)+p Delta-bar_infinity^2(A), with constants depending on max_i||xi_i||_{psi_2}; the tail consequence yields matching sqrt(u) and u deviation scales.
proof_steps: Normalize max_i||xi_i||_{psi_2}<=1 and approximate each A by a coarse net representative pi_l(A).
For the chaining remainder, decouple the quadratic form, use a bilinear chaining lemma, and control diagonal terms by symmetrization, contraction and subgaussian chaining.
For coarse representatives, apply Hanson-Wright to obtain sqrt(p) Delta_4^2 and p Delta_infinity^2 terms.
Combine the pieces into a quadratic inequality for the target moment and solve; use the appendix moment-tail lemma for the tail form.
gaps: The input coordinates must be independent and subgaussian for the cited Hanson-Wright/decoupling route; the result does not assert a generic mixed-tail inequality is always sharp for chaos processes.

constant_dependence.explicit: Theorem 3.5 constants c,C are absolute and unoptimized. Corollary 5.2 retains sigma,K from a uniform Bernstein moment bound. Theorem 5.5 has absolute chaining constants and parameters sigma,K, Delta-bar_{psi_2}; the paper permits sigma=sup_t(m^(-1)sum_i||X_{t i}||_{psi_2}^4)^(1/2), K=sup_{t,i}||X_{t i}||_{psi_2}^2. Theorem 6.5 constants depend on max_i||xi_i||_{psi_2}.
constant_dependence.dependence: Theorem 3.5 does not require independent increments. Empirical-process and chaos corollaries add independence and moment/tail assumptions to produce d_1,d_2 or Hanson-Wright increment bounds. The gamma functionals encode index-set complexity; the base-point moments and metric diameters encode one-point/deviation scales.

endpoint_limits.index_set: The main proof assumes finite T to avoid measurability issues. Infinite T uses finite-subset lattice suprema; ordinary supremum statements require target-specific measurability/separability.
endpoint_limits.tail_parameter: The mixed-tail definition is for u>=0; Theorem 3.5's probability consequence is stated for u>=1, and the proof's chaining union bound starts at u>=2.
endpoint_limits.base_point: The moment theorem includes 2 sup_t||X_t-X_t0||_Lp; it cannot be dropped unless a separate bound is proved.
endpoint_limits.constants: Constants are not sharp; the paper explicitly warns about losses from converting between moments and tails.
endpoint_limits.applications: Theorem 5.5 additionally needs uniform Bernstein control of centered squares; Theorem 6.5 uses independent subgaussian coordinates and matrix-specific radii.

reusable_methods.method: Two-metric chaining for a mixed subgaussian-subexponential increment tail
reusable_methods.transfer: For a center-cube maximal-operator index family, define candidate d_2 and d_1 from small-jump/subgaussian and rare-event/subexponential increments only after proving the mixed-tail inequality for every pair of cubes. Compute both gamma functionals, retain the base-cube term, and show measurability for the chosen cube class. The paper does not identify those metrics for the center-cube maximal operator; that mapping is a project assumption to prove.

reusable_methods.method: Split chaining scales when a statistic changes from subgaussian to subexponential increments
reusable_methods.transfer: Theorem 5.5 splits at a sample-size-dependent scale and controls squared empirical processes via an empirical L2 increment. A center-cube maximal-operator analogue would need a derived threshold, uniform Bernstein control, and a valid increment factorization; none follows from the paper automatically.

reusable_methods.method: Moment-to-tail conversion via optimized Markov bounds
reusable_methods.transfer: Use only after obtaining the full p-moment estimate for all p>=1 and preserve the precise p-dependence. The source's universal constants are non-optimal.

unchecked: The complete extracted text, all proof sections, appendices and references (27 pages) were read. Theorem 3.5 and the displayed mixed-tail/moment formulas were visually checked against PDF pages 7–8 rendered with PyMuPDF.

I checked the partition-intersection cardinality, level telescoping structure, union-bound exponent scale, and separation of gamma_2/gamma_1 and square-root/linear tails from the paper's proof. I did not independently optimize universal constants or reproduce the compressed-sensing application numerically.
Theorem 3.5 is an author-proved result. Any center-cube maximal-operator metric assignment and mixed-tail verification is a migration inference and remains to be proved for that operator.
